question: At a primary health centre OG clinic, which of the following is the MANDATORY clinical register entry for EVERY antenatal visit, as required by HMIS reporting under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) framework?

answers.text: Blood group and Rh factor, haemoglobin, urine albumin, and weight at each visit

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While blood group, Hb, and urine albumin are required investigations, not all are repeated at every single visit. Blood group is recorded once; Hb and urine albumin have defined repeat intervals.

answers.text: Gestational age at the visit, blood pressure, and weight

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Gestational age (calculated from LMP), blood pressure, and weight are the three parameters recorded at EVERY antenatal visit and are the minimum required entries on the MCP card and HMIS register. They form the triage basis for detecting hypertension and undernutrition at each contact.
Incorrect. Ultrasound is recommended at specific gestational ages (10–13 weeks, 18–20 weeks) — not at every ANC visit. Performing or recording USG at every visit is not the HMIS requirement.

answers.text: Full blood count, random blood glucose, and syphilis serology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These investigations are done at the first ANC visit (and glucose is repeated at 24–28 weeks for GDM screening) — not at every visit. They are not the mandatory per-visit register entries.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review HMIS ANC register requirements: gestational age, blood pressure, and weight are the three minimum per-visit entries. Investigations (Hb, urine, glucose, ultrasound) have defined schedules across the four ANC visits.

Correct. At every ANC contact, gestational age, blood pressure, and weight are the minimum mandatory entries. They enable triage for hypertensive disorders and growth monitoring without the resource burden of repeated investigations.
